title: Transformer-Based OCR System for Handwritten Signature Verification in Lawmaking Petitions: A Proof of Concept
content: This work investigates whether handwritten signature verification in citizen-submitted lawmaking petitions can be automated using transformer-based models. Validating each petition requires confirming handwritten personal identifiers and signatures, a manual process that is time-consuming and error-prone due to handwriting variability and high signatory volume. To explore a feasible automated solution, we develop a transformer-based optical character recognition (OCR) pipeline in collaboration with the Parliament of the Canary Islands (Spain). The approach includes designing and evaluating a system for verifying handwritten signatures in petitions while generating synthetic handwriting datasets that comply with privacy regulations, enabling model training without real personal data. We assess the pipeline using a framework adapted to institutional constraints to test its practical application. Results show that the transformer-based method surpasses traditional convolutional recurrent neural networks (CNNs) in accuracy and reliability for handwritten signature verification tasks. We conclude that this method can automate signature verification in lawmaking petitions, reducing manual workload and improving efficiency within parliamentary workflows. This proof of concept demonstrates that transformer-based OCR solutions, specifically using the TrOCR model, can address handwritten signature verification challenges despite real-world data limitations, offering a pathway for future institutional deployment.
